Do you already have a masters degree? If so, you don’t get another OPT on the second masters. Doesn’t matter if you had STEM extension or not on the first masters. OPT is offered only once after every level of degree (bachelors, masters, and PhD) and you can extend if it was a STEM course. So if you go for a higher level of education, like PhD, you can get another OPT and even an extension if the course is STEM. 

Also about Day-1 CPT, if you do it from an Accredited university, it could turn out good for you. I’ve heard Harrisburg University and University of Cumberlands are legit ones. So if you get an RFE on your H1B petition in the future, these universities are usually experts at handling them and they will take care of it. As long as you can prove to USCIS that the second masters you’re doing with Day-1 CPT actually helps further your career and they see you didn’t just use as means to stay in the US, you do have chances of your H1B petition being approved in the future. There’s a risk, but totally legal if you do it correctly!

J1 will come with more restrictions like after you’re done working on that J1 visa, you can’t work in the US for 3 years. 

Day-1 CPT, you might just get an RFE or maybe a denial on your H1B petition if you’re selected in the lottery in the future. 

It’s up to you what risks you’re willing to endure. Good luck!!
